title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: guided OAuth sign-in for connector admins
summary: The roadmap details and most deployment and licensing statements are supported. The staged-rollout path omits the Edit action, and the sources do not establish that no action is required or that these connectors require source-system licences. The description of which account holds the authorisation also goes beyond the documentation.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center connector setup offers guided OAuth authentication for Gong, GitHub and Monday.
claims.quote: Admins can now set up authentication for Gong, GitHub, and Monday connectors using a simplified, faster OAuth experience.

claims.claim: The guided authorisation experience can use a pop-up flow.
claims.quote: Review the workspaces you want to use and the corresponding Microsoft 365 Copilot access level before you choose the install button in the pop-up window.

claims.claim: No action is required for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: streamlined OAuth no action; Copilot connectors OAuth existing connections; streamlined OAuth default connector. Read the roadmap, February/March release-note excerpts and Gong, GitHub and monday deployment pages; none states that no action is required.
claims.fix: Replace 'no action is required, but check who can do it' with 'review who can authorise connectors; Microsoft has not stated what happens to existing connections'.

Complete authentication for supported connectors such as Gong, GitHub, or Monday.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Gong authentication uses OAuth 2.0, Authorize, sign-in and completion of the OAuth consent flow.
claims.quote:
Select 'OAuth 2.0'.
Select Authorize and authenticate to your Gong instance by signing in with a Gong administrator account.
Complete the OAuth consent flow to grant the connector access to the required Gong APIs.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A Gong administrator account authorises the Gong connector.
claims.quote: A Gong administrator must sign in with their Gong credentials to authorize the connector.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: GitHub Cloud Knowledge OAuth setup installs the GitHub Knowledge app in the organisation, enters the organisation name and selects Authorize.
claims.quote:
OAuth (Recommended): To use OAuth authentication:
Install the GitHub Knowledge GitHub app in the GitHub organization.
Choose a display name that helps users recognize the connection.
Enter your organization name.
Choose Authorize to sign in and grant access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The GitHub Cloud Knowledge deployment page marks its OAuth method as preview.
claims.quote: This authentication method is currently in preview.

claims.claim: The recommended monday.com OAuth method installs the Microsoft 365 Copilot monday app in the chosen workspaces and uses Authorize.
claims.quote:
Install the Microsoft 365 Copilot monday app on your monday Workspaces via this link.
Review the workspaces you want to use and the corresponding Microsoft 365 Copilot access level before you choose the install button in the pop-up window.
Choose Authorize to sign in and grant access.

claims.claim: monday.com also supports OAuth 2.0 with a customised app for organisations requiring custom OAuth configuration.
claims.quote:
With OAuth 2.0, you create and configure your own OAuth app in the monday.com Developer Center.
Use this option when your organization requires a custom OAuth app configuration.

claims.claim: Authorising a synced connector grants access used to read source data on an ongoing basis.
claims.quote:
Complete the OAuth consent flow to grant the connector access to the required Gong APIs.
The refresh interval determines how often your data is synced between the data source and the Copilot connector index.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated this roadmap item's default behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: streamlined OAuth default connector; Copilot connectors streamlined OAuth authentication default existing connections migration automatic reauthorize pricing meter. Read roadmap, release-note excerpts and Gong/GitHub/monday setup pages; no arrival default stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited documentation does not say whether existing connections change or migrate to OAuth.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors OAuth existing connections; Copilot connectors streamlined OAuth authentication default existing connections migration automatic reauthorize pricing meter. Read release-note excerpts and Gong, GitHub and monday deployment pages; no migration rule found.

claims.claim: Synced connectors index external source content into Microsoft 365 for Copilot and Search experiences.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors bring external data into Microsoft 365 experiences such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search.
Synced connectors index content from an external data source into the Microsoft 365 substrate on a recurring schedule.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Access Permissions determines whether indexed content respects source access or is visible to everyone.
claims.quote:
Only people with access to this data source: The connector respects source system access control lists (ACLs).
Visible to everyone: The connector grants access to all users in the organization.

claims.claim: Choosing Everyone can lead to oversharing sensitive content.
claims.quote: Incorrect access permission settings, such as granting access to Everyone, can lead to oversharing of sensitive content.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Updating connector access permissions after connection creation is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.claim: Correcting the connection's visibility choice requires deleting and recreating the connection.
claims.quote:
In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection.
Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: The authorisation is held by an account in the source system.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors authorization account OAuth. Read Gong, GitHub Cloud Knowledge and monday deployment pages. They document sign-in, app installation and consent, but do not establish this common account-ownership mechanism.
claims.fix: Remove 'The authorisation is held by an account in the source system:' and start the bullet 'Gong's page asks for a Gong administrator account, and the GitHub page asks for the app to be installed in the GitHub organisation.'

claims.claim: monday.com OAuth consent grants read permissions needed for content ingestion.
claims.quote: During authorization, you sign in to monday.com and grant read permissions required for content ingestion.

claims.claim: Federated connectors with write capabilities are distinct from this synced-connector authentication change.
claims.quote:
Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.
Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.claim: The customised GitHub app on-behalf-of-user authentication method is deprecated.
claims.quote:
Customized GitHub app (on behalf of user) (deprecated)
This authentication method is deprecated and isn't recommended for new connections. Use OAuth or the Customized GitHub app (installation) method instead.

claims.claim: Connector grounding is included without extra charges for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects existing Microsoft 365 entitlement for Search and additional Copilot entitlement for grounding.
claims.quote: Your tenant must have Microsoft 365 licenses. The surfaces available to your users (Microsoft Search, Microsoft 365 Copilot grounding, Copilot Chat agents) and the connector types you can deploy depend on your organization's licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The OAuth setup documentation publishes no separate price or meter for this flow.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors OAuth price; Copilot connectors streamlined OAuth authentication default existing connections migration automatic reauthorize pricing meter. Read connector prerequisites/licensing and Gong, GitHub and monday deployment pages; no OAuth-specific price or meter found.

claims.claim: Source-system licences are a remaining cost required by these connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Gong connector license; GitHub Cloud Knowledge license; monday.com connector license. Read connector prerequisites and all three deployment pages. They require source access and permissions; none specifies a required source-system licence or a resulting licence cost.
claims.fix: Replace 'The cost that remains is admin time and the source-system licences the connector needs, which the source vendor sets.' with 'Plan for admin time and check your source-system licensing terms before deployment.'

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Configuring and deploying Copilot connectors requires the AI administrator role in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Deploying prebuilt synced connectors also requires administrative access to the external service.
claims.quote: In addition, for prebuilt synced connectors (such as Google Drive, Confluence, ServiceNow), you must have admin access to the external service (Google Workspace Super Admin, Confluence Admin).

claims.claim: Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connector > Staged Rollout is the route to changing staged rollout.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
Find the connector that you want to modify.
In the Staged Rollout column, next to Staged, choose Edit.
claims.fix: Change controls[0].ui.path and the corresponding table path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connector > Staged Rollout > Edit'. Staged Rollout is the column; Edit is the action that opens the control, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/staged-rollout.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for this staged-rollout setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection staged rollout limited audience settings API PowerShell. Read staged-rollout documentation and Graph beta externalConnection methods/properties; no operation or property for this setting found.

claims.claim: Staged rollout supports up to 100 users.
claims.quote: You can only add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups to the staged rollout list.

claims.claim: Staged rollout supports up to 15 Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: You can only add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups to the staged rollout list.

claims.claim: Staged rollout requires an AI administrator.
claims.quote: You must be an AI administrator to access this feature.

claims.claim: Staged rollout limits which users and groups see connector results across Search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote:
Staged rollout settings are applicable to all Search and Copilot experiences.
When the rollout finishes, only the users and groups you specified see connector data in results, depending on their permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A pilot can be configured with Rollout to limited audience before Create and later widened from Your Connections.
claims.quote:
Select the toggle next to Rollout to limited audience.
Add the users or security groups that you want to have access to the connector.
Choose Create to create the connection.
You can expand or reduce the scope of the rollout at any time.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Agents > Settings > User access in Microsoft 365 admin center controls access to agents and plugins, including connectors.
claims.quote:
Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts.
Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for the tenant-wide Agents User access setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents Settings User access all users specific users groups Graph API PowerShell; Copilot User access PowerShell agents; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph agent plugin user access settings. Read Agent settings; no operation for this tenant setting found.

claims.claim: User access offers All users, No users and Specific users or groups.
claims.quote:
The setting has three options:
All users
No users
Specific users or groups

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: A connector's staged rollout cannot extend beyond the population allowed by User access.
claims.quote: Agents > Settings > User access also applies to connectors. It sets the maximum population of users who can use any connector, regardless of a connector's own staged rollout.
